description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Purchase' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Real-money in-app purchases (IAP) for Google Play and the Apple App Store. Product catalogue with per-store SKUs (StoreProductIDs), what each purchase grants (Rewards), subscription products that activate a Premium entitlement, audience gates and purchase limits, plus per-store receipt-verification settings. Distinct from Store (in-game shop paid with virtual currency) and from Premium (which describes the entitlement itself, while this describes how it is sold in the stores). Contains NO secrets: the Google service-account JSON and the App Store Server API key are referenced by TitleSecrets entry name only; the Play licensing public key and Apple root certificates are public by nature and live here.

x-enum-descriptions: Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

IapPresetRegistry.description: Registry of reusable IAP product blocks. Same purpose as Character/Leaderboard presets: a rule is described once and reused by many products.

IapProductDefinition.description: Definition of a single real-money product.

AssetPaths.description: Product assets (icon, banner). Key = asset slug, value = path or URL.

CustomParams.description: Free-form product parameters for game code (e.g. "BadgeText", "SortOrder"). Not interpreted by the platform.

Enabled.description: Product is on sale. false = withdrawn (validating old receipts is still possible for non-consumable restore).

Name.description: Display name shown in the client / admin.

Presets.description: References to reusable blocks in PurchaseDefinitions.Presets.

PriceUsdCents.description: Declared price in USD cents — for analytics and default storefront display ONLY. The amount actually paid comes from the receipt; the server never treats this field as the source of truth about a payment.

ProductID.description: Our stable product identifier. Never change after publication — player purchase counters and transaction ledger entries reference it.

Refund.description: What to do when the store refunds this product to the player. Unset = fall back to PurchaseDefinitions.Refund and then to the platform default. Read it only through IapRefundDefaults.

Rewards.description: What the player receives on purchase. For Subscription products this is the welcome grant on first activation; renewals are handled by IapSubscriptionBinding.RenewalRewards. Premium mechanics (PremiumBonuses / PremiumTiers) apply as everywhere else.

Rules.description: Product availability rules: sales window, audience gate, purchase limits.

StoreProductIDs.description: Product SKU per store. Key = IapStore name, value = the STORE-side product identifier (Google Play product ID / Apple product identifier). The server maps a receipt to our product through this dictionary: SKU inside the receipt → ProductID. Duplicate SKUs across products are not allowed.

Subscription.description: Premium subscription binding. Required for Subscription products, ignored otherwise.

TelegramStarsPrice.description: Price in Telegram Stars (XTR, whole number). Unlike other stores WE set this price: the server issues the invoice and Telegram charges exactly this amount, so the field is the source of truth about the payment and the amount in the payment update is checked against it. Unset or not positive = the product is not sold in Telegram.

Type.description: Product type: consumable, non-consumable or subscription.

IapProductPresets.description: Product references to reusable blocks. Resolved by PurchaseConfigResolver on the engine side; a non-existent PresetID is treated as "no preset" and never throws.

Refund.description: Refund policy preset (IapPresetRegistry.Refund). Merged FIELD-WISE like Rules: preset is the base, inline product fields override it, and PresetBinding.Remove drops preset fields by name ("ResourceAction", "RevokeEntitlement", "BlockFuturePurchases").

Rewards.description: Rewards preset (IapPresetRegistry.Rewards). Whole-block: if the product has its own Rewards it wins and the preset is not merged (a reward grant has no key to merge by).

Rules.description: Rules preset (IapPresetRegistry.Rules). Merged FIELD-WISE: preset is the base, inline product fields override it, and PresetBinding.Remove drops preset fields by name ("StartUtc", "EndUtc", "Gate", "Limits").

IapProductRules.description: Product availability rules. An empty object means "on sale to everyone, always".

Gate.description: Who the product is available to — unified SegmentGate. null/empty = everyone. IMPORTANT: the gate is checked at grant time, while the player pays in the store BEFORE the server learns about the purchase, so a gated product must be hidden by the client storefront. A gate rejection is recorded in the transaction ledger for support.

Limits.description: Purchase limits: TotalCap = lifetime, DailyCap = per UTC day. 0 on an axis = unlimited. Like the gate, enforced at grant time — see the warning on Gate.

StartUtc.description: Sales start (UTC). null = from the beginning.

x-enum-descriptions: Consumable: can be bought repeatedly; each purchase grants Rewards again (currency packs, bundles).
Non-consumable: granted once forever (remove ads, content unlock). Re-validating the same receipt (restore) does not grant twice but reports ownership back to the client.
Subscription: activates a premium entitlement (IapSubscriptionBinding.PremiumID) for the period reported by the store. Renewals and revocations arrive via server notifications.

IapRefundPolicy.description: What the platform does when a purchase is refunded. Every field is nullable on purpose: the merge rule is "unset = inherit from the level above, set = final, including false". Read these fields only through IapRefundDefaults. Priority: product → product preset → title-level PurchaseDefinitions.Refund → platform default.

BlockFuturePurchases.description: Forbid this player from buying THIS product again after a refund. Unset = false. Enforced where purchase limits are — at grant time — so the player pays in the store and gets a rejection recorded in the ledger. Pair it with a storefront that hides the blocked product (the flag is reported in IapProductAvailability).

ResourceAction.description: What to do with the granted resources. Unset = Keep.

RevokeEntitlement.description: Revoke entitlements: expire the premium immediately for a subscription, drop ownership for a non-consumable (ads come back, content locks). Unset = for subscriptions fall back to IapSubscriptionBinding.RevokeOnRefund (kept for already-configured titles), for other types the default is true.

x-enum-descriptions: Take nothing back — only mark the refund in the ledger and (if configured) revoke the entitlement. This is how the platform behaved historically and remains the default.

Claw back what was granted but never below the floor: only the remaining amount is deducted. If the player spent everything, nothing is deducted and the operation still succeeds. Safe: inventory invariants stay intact.

Claw back the full amount, allowing the currency balance to go below CurrencyDefinition.Economy.MinBalance — including negative. The debt is paid off by later grants: while the balance is negative the player effectively receives nothing. Applies to CURRENCIES only — items have no negative quantity and are always deducted up to what is present. Also drops the race guard on the deduction, since the point of the mode is that it goes through regardless of the balance.
Google Play Billing (Android).
Apple App Store / StoreKit (iOS, macOS, tvOS).

Telegram Stars — payment in Telegram Stars (mini apps and bots). The client holds no receipt: the server creates the invoice and Telegram reports the payment to the title bot's webhook. Product price is IapProductDefinition.TelegramStarsPrice.

IapStoreDefinition.description: Per-store settings: how a receipt is verified and how a purchase is acknowledged.

AcknowledgePurchases.description: GOOGLE ONLY. Acknowledge the purchase in the store after granting rewards (acknowledge / consume). Without acknowledgement Google auto-refunds after three days. Requires the networked verification mode or separately configured Play Developer API access. There is nothing to acknowledge on Apple — the client closes the transaction through StoreKit and the server takes no part in it, so the value is IGNORED for the Apple store.

Enabled.description: Accepting purchases from this store is enabled.

IssuerID.description: Apple App Store Server API: Issuer ID from App Store Connect. Not a secret. The signing private key (.p8) is addressed via SecretName.

KeyID.description: Apple App Store Server API: Key ID of the issued key. Not a secret.

NotificationPackageName.description: Expected package in this store's server notifications. Empty = use PackageName. A separate field is needed by titles whose notifications arrive from a different package (e.g. after an app migration).

PackageName.description: Android package name (com.example.game) or iOS bundle ID. Compared against the value inside the receipt when IapValidationSettings.RequirePackageMatch is on.

PlayPublicKey.description: Google Play: the app's RSA licensing public key (base64 from Play Console, "Licensing & in-app billing"). Public by nature — it verifies the receipt signature and cannot be used to forge one. Required by the LocalSignature mode.

RequireCertificateChain.description: Require a full certificate chain up to the Apple root (built into the platform, not configurable). false verifies only the leaf signature — acceptable on a test bench, but in production it means "accept a receipt signed by anyone".

SecretName.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the store's shared secret: the Google Play service-account JSON (Play Developer API access) or the App Store shared secret. The value itself is never stored here and never leaves the server.

StoreID.description: Store identifier; must match the key in PurchaseDefinitions.Stores.

IapSubscriptionBinding.description: Link between an IAP product and a platform premium subscription. Activation writes into UserDataDocument.Premium.Subscriptions[PremiumID] — the same container used by Premium.PurchaseWithResources and ActivateTrial, so every premium gate works with IAP subscriptions unchanged.

FallbackDurationDays.description: Duration in days used when the store did not report an expiration date. 0 = fall back to PremiumDefinition.DurationDays. The normal path is expiresDate from the receipt — that is the truth about the period.

PremiumID.description: PremiumID in cfg.Premium.Definitions activated by this subscription. A Subscription product without a valid PremiumID would charge the player and grant nothing.

RenewalRewards.description: What to grant on EACH renewal (monthly subscriber bonus). null = entitlement only, no resources. Renewals arrive via store server notifications.

RevokeOnRefund.description: Revoke the premium entitlement on refund/revoke notifications. true = the subscription is expired immediately; false = the entitlement lives out the paid period (kinder to the player, costlier for the economy).

IapValidationSettings.description: Receipt validation rules shared by all stores.

AllowSandbox.description: Accept sandbox / test-track purchases. Usually false in production: the sandbox issues genuine receipts for zero payment.

MaxPurchaseAgeDays.description: Maximum purchase age in days still accepted for a FIRST grant. 0 = unlimited. Guards against replaying a year-old receipt onto a fresh account; does not affect non-consumable restore (which confirms ownership without granting).

MaxReceiptsPerBatch.description: How many receipts one ValidatePurchasesBatch (restore) call accepts. Clamped by the platform BatchSupport.MaxBatchSize. 0 = platform default.

RefundCheckHorizonDays.description: For how many days after a purchase the platform keeps asking Apple whether it was refunded. 0 = always ask. Apple ONLY: there refunds are discovered with a per-customer request, so a long-time payer is polled forever, while Google has no per-player refund query at all and uses one app-wide pass whose cost does not depend on the player count. The trade-off: a refund issued after the horizon is never seen. Do not set it below 90 days — that is the usual window for Apple billing disputes.

RejectCrossUserReceipts.description: Reject a receipt whose TransactionID was already granted to ANOTHER player. true is the standard behavior; the flag exists for titles where account merging makes moving a purchase between UserIDs a normal operation.

RequirePackageMatch.description: Require the package name / bundle ID inside the receipt to match IapStoreDefinition.PackageName. Disable only during a package migration.

x-enum-descriptions: Google Play: the receipt's RSA signature is checked against the licensing public key (IapStoreDefinition.PlayPublicKey). No network, no quotas, no secrets. Blind to refunds and revocations — those arrive via server notifications.
Apple: StoreKit 2 signed transaction (JWS ES256 with an x5c chain up to the Apple root). No network. Like LocalSignature, it does not see refunds by itself.

Call the store's server API: Google Play Developer API (purchases.products.get / purchases.subscriptionsv2.get) or Apple App Store Server API. The most authoritative answer (sees refunds, revocations, current subscription status) but depends on third-party availability and quotas.
Apple: legacy verifyReceipt (base64 app receipt). Deprecated by Apple; kept for StoreKit 1 titles that have not moved to signed transactions.

Verification disabled: the receipt is accepted as-is. FOR TEST BENCHES AND DEBUGGING ONLY — in this mode any player can grant themselves any product. The server marks every such purchase in the transaction ledger.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

PremiumTierBonus.description: Percentage bonus on ResourceGrant.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 + Bonus) with Math.Ceiling rounding. Applies only to Standard; in Replace mode the bonused Standard is wiped when any PremiumTier matches. Best matching tier wins, bonuses do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierDiscount.

Bonus.description: Bonus as a SHARE: 0.1 = +10%, 1.0 = double (x2). Empty or 0 = no bonus. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

PresetBinding.description: Wiring for one preset block of an entity: a reference into the module's preset registry + optional keys to drop. Reusable Core container, one per preset-able block, held inside the entity's Presets container. Replaces the former scattered flat *PresetID / *Remove fields. Combination is data-driven, no mode (PresetResolver): no PresetID -> inline only; preset + empty inline -> preset; preset + inline -> merge (preset base + inline overrides/adds by key), Remove drops keys. For a single object (Character Equipment) there is nothing to key-merge, so inline wins when both are present.

PresetID.description: Preset key in the module registry (e.g. LeaderboardDefinitions.Presets.Milestones[PresetID]). Empty/null = preset unused (inline layer only).

Remove.description: Keys removed from the merged result. Dictionary key for dictionaries; element key for keyed lists (Rank / SlotID / RuleID). null = remove nothing. Ignored when no preset is set.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Coin, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account. Requires only Amount — the price in whole Coin. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCoinPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted only by the store (Store.Purchase) for now; allowed only in Consume.

ResourceGrant.description: Grant direction container for ResourceOperation. Two independent premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumBonuses applies a percentage uplift to Standard (single best tier wins, no stack), and PremiumTiers provides structurally different rewards governed by cfg.Reward.TierRewards (Additive or Replace mode; in Replace the bonused Standard is wiped). Both mechanisms can be used together or independently.

PremiumBonuses.description: Percentage uplift on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 + Bonus)). Wiped under Mode=Replace if any PremiumTier matches.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different rewards for premium players (different ItemID/Target/...). Governed by global cfg.Reward.TierRewards.RewardMode (Additive/Replace) and RewardStackLowerTiers.

Standard.description: Base — what to grant to all players including F2P.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).

value.description: Real-money in-app purchase (IAP) configuration for Google Play and Apple App Store. Product catalog (what the player buys and receives) is separated from per-store settings (how a receipt is verified). One product can be sold in both stores under different SKUs via StoreProductIDs.

Enabled.description: Master switch for the whole IAP subsystem. When false the server rejects every receipt validation regardless of per-product and per-store settings.

Presets.description: Reusable product configuration blocks (rewards and rules).

Products.description: Product catalog. Key = IapProductDefinition.ProductID (OUR stable identifier, not the store SKU).

Refund.description: Default refund policy for every product of the title. A product overrides it with its own Refund block or a preset. When unset the platform defaults apply.

Validation.description: Validation rules shared by all stores.
